context:
Goal: the TestFlight dry run can sign the build with your Apple Development certificate.
Why yours: the certificate sits in your login Keychain and the repo secrets take your own GitHub login, and no cloud session reaches either (measured 2026-11-16, list_computer_folders returned no usable folder on MacBook-Pro-2: Documents, joyous and Developer all report not_available).
What went wrong: the earlier commands set ASC_DEV_CERT_P12 empty twice. First the command ran in the wrong folder, then the file was gone, and a pipe hid the error. You have since deleted the old export, and the P12 secret is empty now. The new command checks each step and stops on the first error.
The secret holds the file in base64, and the workflow reads it that way (.github/workflows/testflight.yml, line 7).
What runs next: pull request 344 makes the TestFlight run fail at once when the P12 secret is empty, instead of signing without it. When it has landed and the two secrets are set, the coordinator starts one dry run and the lane reads its log.
The bash block was run against a stand-in for gh in bash, and not in zsh. The PowerShell block is for a Windows machine and is not tested here.
ref: step testflight-p12-reset (owner act: re-export the cert and re-set its two secrets); lane testflight-identity (the TestFlight identity lane); PR 344 (fail on an empty P12)
steps: Open Keychain Access on your Mac. In the login keychain, under My Certificates, choose the Apple Development entry and export it as dev.p12 to your Desktop. Pick a password, and remember it.
Paste the command below in a terminal on your Mac. On Windows, copy dev.p12 to your Desktop first and use the PowerShell block.
Type the same password when it asks for the passphrase of dev.p12. It prints the two secret names when both are set, and stops with a message on the first error.
title: Re-export the Apple Development certificate and re-set its two repo secrets
